questions.question: A box-and-whisker plot has its whiskers ending at 12 and 40, the left edge of the box at 18, the right edge at 30, and the line inside the box at 24. What is the median of the data?
questions.explanation: The vertical line inside the box marks the median. Here that line is at 24, so the median is 24.

questions.question: For the same plot (minimum 12, Q1 = 18, median = 24, Q3 = 30, maximum 40), what is the range of the data?
questions.explanation: Range = maximum - minimum = 40 - 12 = 28. (12 would be the interquartile range, not the range.)

questions.question: A box plot shows Q1 = 18 and Q3 = 30, with median 24. What is the interquartile range, and what does the box itself represent?

options.A: IQR = 12; the box holds the middle 50% of the data
options.B: IQR = 12; the box holds all of the data
options.C: IQR = 6; the box holds the middle 25% of the data
options.D: IQR = 28; the box holds the middle 50% of the data

questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 30 - 18 = 12. The box stretches from Q1 to Q3, which contains the middle 50% of the values.

questions.question: The test scores of 200 students are summarised by a box plot with minimum 55, Q1 = 68, median = 74, Q3 = 85 and maximum 96. About how many students scored more than 74?
questions.explanation: The median splits the data into two halves, so about half the 200 students, i.e. 100 students, scored above 74.

questions.question: A box plot summarises 80 data values. How many values lie between Q1 and the maximum, and how many lie between Q1 and Q3?
questions.explanation: Q1 to the maximum covers the top three quarters: 0.75 x 80 = 60 values. Q1 to Q3 covers the middle half: 0.50 x 80 = 40 values.

questions.question: A data set has Q1 = 22 and Q3 = 34. Using the rule that a value is an outlier if it lies more than 1.5 x IQR beyond a quartile, what is the upper outlier boundary, and is 55 an outlier?
questions.explanation: IQR = 34 - 22 = 12, so 1.5 x IQR = 18. Upper boundary = Q3 + 18 = 34 + 18 = 52. Since 55 > 52, it is an outlier.

questions.question: Two classes are compared. Class A: Q1 = 65, median = 70, Q3 = 75. Class B: Q1 = 50, median = 70, Q3 = 90. Which statement is best supported?

options.A: Class A performed better on average than Class B
options.B: Class B performed better on average than Class A
options.C: The two classes have the same typical score, but Class B's scores are far more spread out
options.D: Class B must contain the single highest score in the school

questions.explanation: Both medians are 70, so the typical score is the same. Class A's IQR is 10 while Class B's is 40, so Class B's middle scores are much more spread out. Nothing about the maxima is given.

questions.question: Which five-number summary correctly describes the data set 4, 7, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 25?
questions.explanation: With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (12 + 15)/2 = 13.5. Q1 is the median of 4, 7, 9, 12 = (7 + 9)/2 = 8. Q3 is the median of 15, 18, 21, 25 = (18 + 21)/2 = 19.5.

questions.question: A box plot of 40 values has minimum 20, Q1 = 30, median = 38, Q3 = 50 and maximum 80. In which quarter are the data values packed most tightly together, and why?

options.A: From the minimum to Q1, because that whisker looks short
options.B: From Q1 to the median, because 10 values are squeezed into a width of only 8
options.C: From Q3 to the maximum, because that quarter has the largest width
options.D: The data are equally spread in all four quarters because each holds 10 values

questions.explanation: Each quarter contains 10 of the 40 values. The widths are 10, 8, 12 and 30. The quarter from Q1 to the median is narrowest (width 8) yet still holds 10 values, so it is the most densely packed.

questions.question: A data set of 12 values has the five-number summary: min 5, Q1 = 11, median 16, Q3 = 23, max 40. Every value is first increased by 3 and then doubled. What is the interquartile range of the new data set?
questions.explanation: Original IQR = 23 - 11 = 12. Adding 3 to every value shifts both quartiles equally and leaves the spread unchanged; doubling multiplies every distance by 2. So the new IQR = 2 x 12 = 24. (Checking directly: new Q1 = 2(11+3) = 28, new Q3 = 2(23+3) = 52, difference 24.)

questions.question: A circle graph shows the favourite subject of 200 students: Maths 30%, Science 25%, English 20%, History 15%, Art 10%. Which subject was chosen by the greatest number of students?
questions.explanation: The largest sector is the one with the largest percentage. Maths has 30%, which is more than any other subject.

questions.question: Using the same circle graph (200 students; Science = 25%), how many students chose Science?
A circle graph shows how 400 people travel to work. The 'Walk' sector represents 60 people. What percentage of the circle graph is the 'Walk' sector?
questions.explanation: 60/400 = 0.15 = 15%. This reverses the usual direction: here the count is given and the percentage must be found.

questions.question: In the subject circle graph (200 students; Maths 30%, Art 10%), how many more students chose Maths than Art?
questions.explanation: The difference is 30% - 10% = 20% of the students, and 20% of 200 = 40 students. (60 and 20 are the separate counts, not their difference.)

questions.question: A circle graph of holiday destinations has five sectors: Beach 28%, Hills 22%, City 17%, Village 13% and Other. What percentage is 'Other', and what is the size of its central angle?
questions.explanation: The listed sectors total 28 + 22 + 17 + 13 = 80%, so Other = 100 - 80 = 20%. Its angle = 0.20 x 360 = 72 degrees.

questions.question: In the subject circle graph (200 students; Science 25%, English 20%), the Science and English sectors are combined into one 'Languages and Science' sector. How many students does this sector represent, and what central angle would it have?
questions.explanation: Combined percentage = 25 + 20 = 45%. Students = 0.45 x 200 = 90. Central angle = 0.45 x 360 = 162 degrees.

questions.question: In a circle graph showing how students travel to school, the 'Bus' sector has a central angle of 126 degrees and represents 84 students. How many students are in the whole survey?
questions.explanation: The Bus sector is 126/360 = 35% of the circle. If 35% of the total is 84, the total = 84 / 0.35 = 240 students. The reasoning runs backwards from a sector to the whole.

questions.question: School A has 800 students and its circle graph shows 25% cycle to school. School B has 500 students and its circle graph shows 35% cycle to school. Which school has more cyclists, and by how many?

options.D: They have the same number of cyclists

questions.explanation: School A: 0.25 x 800 = 200 cyclists. School B: 0.35 x 500 = 175 cyclists. School A has 200 - 175 = 25 more, even though its percentage is smaller, because the two circle graphs represent different totals.

questions.question: A family's monthly spending is shown in a circle graph: Rent 35%, Food 20%, Transport 15%, Savings 10%, Other 20%. The amount spent on Rent is 6250 rupees more than the amount put into Savings. How much is spent on Food and Transport together?
questions.explanation: Rent - Savings = 35% - 10% = 25% of the total, and this equals 6250, so the total = 6250 / 0.25 = 25000. Food + Transport = 20% + 15% = 35% of 25000 = 8750 rupees.

questions.question: A circle graph has exactly four sectors. The second sector's angle is twice the first, the third is three times the first, and the fourth is 45 degrees more than the first. If the graph represents 720 people, how many people are represented by the largest sector?
questions.explanation: Let the first angle be x. Then x + 2x + 3x + (x + 45) = 360, so 7x = 315 and x = 45. The angles are 45, 90, 135 and 90 degrees, so the largest is 135 degrees. That is 135/360 = 37.5% of the circle, and 0.375 x 720 = 270 people.

questions.question: A histogram of test scores has these bars: 0-9 (4 students), 10-19 (8), 20-29 (12), 30-39 (11), 40-49 (5). Which interval contains the most students?
questions.explanation: The tallest bar has the greatest frequency. The 20-29 interval has 12 students, more than any other interval.

questions.question: Using the same histogram (0-9: 4, 10-19: 8, 20-29: 12, 30-39: 11, 40-49: 5), how many students scored in the 30-39 interval?
questions.explanation: Read the height of the bar over 30-39: it is 11 students.

questions.question: For the same histogram, how many students took the test in total?
questions.explanation: Add all the bar heights: 4 + 8 + 12 + 11 + 5 = 40 students.

questions.question: The scores of 40 students are grouped as 0-9: 4, 10-19: 8, 20-29: 12, 30-39: 11, 40-49: 5. The teacher wants to know how many students scored below 20. What is that number?
questions.explanation: 'Below 20' covers the 0-9 and 10-19 intervals: 4 + 8 = 12 students.

questions.question: For the same grouped data (total 40 students, with 12 in the 20-29 interval), what percentage of students scored in the 20-29 interval, and what percentage scored 30 or above?
For the grouped data 0-9: 4, 10-19: 8, 20-29: 12, 30-39: 11, 40-49: 5 (40 values in all), which interval contains the median?

options.D: The median cannot lie in any single interval

questions.explanation: With 40 values the median is between the 20th and 21st values. Cumulative frequencies are 4, 12, 24, 35, 40, so both the 20th and 21st values fall in the 20-29 interval.

questions.question: Using the same histogram, which statement is definitely supported by the data?

options.B: More than half of the students scored below 30
options.C: The highest score in the class was 49

questions.explanation: Students scoring below 30 number 4 + 8 + 12 = 24 out of 40, which is 60% - more than half. A histogram does not reveal individual values, the exact maximum, or the exact mean.

questions.question: Estimate the mean score from the grouped data 0-9: 4, 10-19: 8, 20-29: 12, 30-39: 11, 40-49: 5, using the midpoint of each interval.
questions.explanation: Midpoints are 4.5, 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5. Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 18 + 116 + 294 + 379.5 + 222.5 = 1030. Estimated mean = 1030/40 = 25.75.

questions.question: A frequency table records 50 observations: 0-9: 6, 10-19: missing, 20-29: 14, 30-39: 10, 40-49: 12. What percentage of the observations are below 20?
questions.explanation: The known frequencies total 6 + 14 + 10 + 12 = 42, so the missing frequency is 50 - 42 = 8. Observations below 20 = 6 + 8 = 14, and 14/50 = 28%.

questions.question: A histogram uses the intervals 0-10, 10-20, 20-30 and 30-40 (midpoints 5, 15, 25, 35) with frequencies 5, x, 10 and 5. The estimated mean of the data is exactly 20. What is x?
questions.explanation: Sum of (midpoint x frequency) = 5(5) + 15x + 25(10) + 35(5) = 25 + 15x + 250 + 175 = 450 + 15x. Total frequency = 20 + x. Setting (450 + 15x)/(20 + x) = 20 gives 450 + 15x = 400 + 20x, so 50 = 5x and x = 10.

questions.question: Four points are marked on a number line at -7, -2, 0 and 3. Which point lies farthest to the left?
questions.explanation: On a number line, values increase to the right, so the smallest number is farthest left. -7 is the smallest of the four.

questions.question: What is the distance between the points -4 and 5 on a number line?
questions.explanation: Distance is always positive: |5 - (-4)| = |9| = 9 units. (1 comes from adding the numbers instead of subtracting.)

questions.question: A marker starts at -6 on a number line, moves 10 units to the right, then 4 units to the left. Where does it end?
questions.explanation: -6 + 10 = 4, then 4 - 4 = 0. The marker ends at the origin.

questions.question: A diver is 18 metres below sea level, so her position is -18 on a vertical number line. She rises 7 metres, then descends 5 metres. What is her position now?
questions.explanation: Rising is positive and descending is negative: -18 + 7 = -11, then -11 - 5 = -16. She is 16 metres below sea level.

questions.question: Point A is at -9 and point B is at 5 on a number line. What is the coordinate of the midpoint of AB?
questions.explanation: Midpoint = (-9 + 5)/2 = -4/2 = -2. Check: the distance from -9 to -2 is 7, and from -2 to 5 is also 7.

questions.question: Which two points on a number line are exactly 5 units away from the point 2?
questions.explanation: The condition is |x - 2| = 5, so x - 2 = 5 or x - 2 = -5, giving x = 7 or x = -3. Both lie 5 units from 2.

questions.question: Point A is at -5. Point B lies to the right of A and the distance AB is 12 units. Which statement is true?

options.A: B is at 7, and A is closer to zero than B is
options.B: B is at 7, and B is closer to zero than A is
options.C: B is at -17, and B is closer to zero than A is
options.D: B is at 17, and A and B are equally far from zero

questions.explanation: Moving 12 units right from -5 gives B = -5 + 12 = 7. Distance from zero: A is |−5| = 5 units away, B is |7| = 7 units away, so A is closer to zero.

questions.question: Points P and Q are at -8 and 10 on a number line. Point R lies between them so that PR : RQ = 1 : 2. What is the coordinate of R?
questions.explanation: PQ = 10 - (-8) = 18 units. Splitting 18 in the ratio 1 : 2 gives PR = 6 and RQ = 12. So R = -8 + 6 = -2.

questions.question: A grasshopper starts at 4 on a number line. It hops 7 left, then 3 right, then 6 left, then 11 right. Compare the total distance it hopped with its final distance from its starting point.

options.A: The total distance is greater by 26 units
options.B: The total distance is greater by 22 units
options.D: The final distance is greater by 1 unit

questions.explanation: Final position = 4 - 7 + 3 - 6 + 11 = 5, so the distance from the start (4) is 1 unit. Total distance hopped = 7 + 3 + 6 + 11 = 27 units. The difference is 27 - 1 = 26 units.

questions.question: On a number line, A is at -6 and B is at 14. Point C lies on segment AB so that AC = 3 x CB. What is the coordinate of the midpoint of AC?
questions.explanation: AB = 14 - (-6) = 20. Since AC = 3 x CB, the segment splits in the ratio 3 : 1, so AC = 15 and C = -6 + 15 = 9. The midpoint of AC is (-6 + 9)/2 = 1.5.

questions.question: On a scatter plot, the points generally rise from the lower left to the upper right. What kind of association do the two variables show?
questions.explanation: When one variable increases as the other increases, the cloud of points slopes upward, which is a positive association.

questions.question: A scatter plot compares hours studied (x) with test score (y). One plotted point is (5, 72). What does this point mean?

options.A: A student studied 72 hours and scored 5
options.B: A student studied 5 hours and scored 72
options.D: The average score is 72 for all students

questions.explanation: In an ordered pair the first coordinate is the x-value (hours studied = 5) and the second is the y-value (score = 72).

questions.question: A scatter plot of hours studied against score contains the points (1, 52), (2, 58), (3, 64), (4, 70), (9, 41) and (5, 76). Which point is an outlier?
questions.explanation: All the other points follow a clear upward pattern of about +6 points per extra hour. The point (9, 41) sits far away from that pattern, so it is the outlier.

questions.question: A scatter plot compares the age of a used car (in years) with its selling price. The points fall steadily from left to right. What does the plot suggest?

options.A: Older cars tend to sell for more
options.B: Older cars tend to sell for less
options.D: All cars of the same age sell for the same price

questions.explanation: A downward trend means that as age increases, price decreases - a negative association. The plot shows a tendency, not an exact rule for every car.

questions.question: The line of best fit for a scatter plot of hours studied (x) and score (y) is y = 4x + 50. What score does the line predict for a student who studies 7 hours?
For the line of best fit y = 4x + 50, where x is hours studied and y is test score, what do the slope and the y-intercept mean in this situation?

options.A: Each extra hour of study is associated with about 4 more points; a student who studies 0 hours is predicted to score about 50
options.B: Each extra hour of study is associated with about 50 more points; the maximum score is 4
options.C: Studying 4 hours guarantees a score of 50
options.D: The scores increase by 4 points every 50 hours

questions.explanation: The slope 4 is the predicted change in y for a 1-unit increase in x, and the intercept 50 is the predicted y-value when x = 0.

questions.question: A scatter plot shows a strong positive association between the number of ice creams sold in a town and the number of sunburn cases reported. Which conclusion is justified?

options.B: Sunburn causes people to buy ice cream
options.C: The two quantities tend to rise and fall together, possibly because both increase in hot, sunny weather
options.D: Because the association is strong, one variable must cause the other

questions.explanation: A scatter plot can show association but not causation. A third factor - hot, sunny weather - plausibly drives both quantities.

questions.question: The line of best fit is y = 4x + 50. A student who studied 7 hours actually scored 82. What is the residual for this student, and where does the point lie relative to the line?

options.A: Residual -4; the point lies below the line
options.B: Residual +4; the point lies above the line
options.C: Residual +32; the point lies above the line
options.D: Residual 0; the point lies on the line

questions.explanation: Predicted score = 4(7) + 50 = 78. Residual = actual - predicted = 82 - 78 = +4. A positive residual means the point sits above the line of best fit.

questions.question: A line of best fit passes through the points (2, 58) and (6, 74) on a scatter plot of hours studied against score. What score does this line predict for 10 hours of study?

For a set of bivariate data, the mean of x is 6 and the mean of y is 41. The least-squares line of best fit has slope 3.5 and, as always, passes through the point of means. What value does the line predict when x = 12?
questions.explanation: The line passes through (6, 41), so 41 = 3.5(6) + b = 21 + b, giving b = 20 and y = 3.5x + 20. At x = 12: y = 42 + 20 = 62.

questions.question: A stem-and-leaf plot (stems are tens, leaves are ones) shows: 1 | 2 5 8; 2 | 0 3 3 7 9; 3 | 1 4 6; 4 | 0 2. What is the smallest value in the data set?
questions.explanation: The first stem is 1 and its first leaf is 2, so the smallest value is 12.

questions.question: Using the same plot (1 | 2 5 8; 2 | 0 3 3 7 9; 3 | 1 4 6; 4 | 0 2), how many data values are in the twenties?
questions.explanation: The stem 2 has the leaves 0, 3, 3, 7, 9 - that is 5 values (20, 23, 23, 27, 29).

questions.question: For the same stem-and-leaf plot, how many data values are there in total, and what is the range?
questions.explanation: Counting the leaves: 3 + 5 + 3 + 2 = 13 values. Range = largest - smallest = 42 - 12 = 30.

questions.question: The plot 1 | 2 5 8; 2 | 0 3 3 7 9; 3 | 1 4 6; 4 | 0 2 records the ages of 13 club members. What is the mode of the ages?
questions.explanation: A repeated leaf on the same stem means a repeated value. The stem 2 has the leaf 3 twice, so 23 occurs twice and every other value occurs once. The mode is 23.

questions.question: For the same 13 values, what is the median?
questions.explanation: A stem-and-leaf plot is already in order: 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42. With 13 values the median is the 7th value, which is 27.

questions.question: Using the same ordered data (12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42), what is the interquartile range?
questions.explanation: Excluding the median (27), the lower half is 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23 so Q1 = (18 + 20)/2 = 19. The upper half is 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42 so Q3 = (34 + 36)/2 = 35. IQR = 35 - 19 = 16.

questions.question: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot compares two classes. Class X leaves cluster on the stems 6 and 7, while Class Y leaves are spread across the stems 4 to 9, with roughly the same number of values in each class. Which statement is best supported?

options.A: Class X has a higher median than Class Y
options.B: Class X scores are more consistent, while Class Y scores vary much more widely
options.C: Class Y has more students than Class X
options.D: Class X contains the single highest score

questions.explanation: Clustering on two stems means a small spread for Class X; leaves across six stems means a large spread for Class Y. The plot as described says nothing conclusive about which median is higher, the counts, or the single highest score.

questions.question: A new value, 33, is added to the data 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42. What is the median of the 14 values now?
questions.explanation: The new ordered list is 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 33, 34, 36, 40, 42. With 14 values the median is the mean of the 7th and 8th: (27 + 29)/2 = 28.

questions.question: In the plot for 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42, the largest value is corrected from 42 to 62. Which measures change?

options.A: The mean and the range change; the median and the mode stay the same
options.B: All four of mean, median, mode and range change
options.D: The median and the mode change; the mean and the range stay the same

questions.explanation: The total increases by 20, so the mean rises. The range becomes 62 - 12 = 50 instead of 30. The value stays the largest, so the 7th value (27) is still the median, and 23 is still the only repeated value.

questions.question: The 13 values 12, 15, 18, 20, 23, 23, 27, 29, 31, 34, 36, 40, 42 are shown in a stem-and-leaf plot. One more value is added so that the median of the 14 values becomes exactly 28. Which value could have been added?
questions.explanation: With 14 values the median is the mean of the 7th and 8th. Adding a value of at least 29 leaves the 7th and 8th as 27 and 29, giving (27 + 29)/2 = 28, so 35 works. Adding 28 gives (27 + 28)/2 = 27.5; adding 27 gives (27 + 27)/2 = 27; adding 24 shifts the pair to 23 and 27, giving 25.

questions.question: A shop's sales table shows: Pens - Mon 12, Tue 15, Wed 9, Thu 14; Books - Mon 7, Tue 4, Wed 11, Thu 8; Bags - Mon 5, Tue 6, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many pens were sold on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: Find the Pens row and the Tuesday column. The entry where they meet is 15.

questions.question: Using the same table, how many pens were sold over all four days?
questions.explanation: Add the Pens row: 12 + 15 + 9 + 14 = 50 pens.

questions.question: Using the same sales table, which day had the greatest total number of items sold?
questions.explanation: Column totals: Mon 12 + 7 + 5 = 24, Tue 15 + 4 + 6 = 25, Wed 9 + 11 + 3 = 23, Thu 14 + 8 + 6 = 28. Thursday is highest.

questions.question: In the same table the Bags row reads 5, 6, 3, 6. Each bag sells for 150 rupees. How much money did bag sales bring in over the four days?
questions.explanation: Total bags = 5 + 6 + 3 + 6 = 20. Money = 20 x 150 = 3000 rupees.

questions.question: The Books row of the same table reads 7, 4, 11, 8. What is the mean number of books sold per day, and on how many days were sales above that mean?
questions.explanation: Total books = 7 + 4 + 11 + 8 = 30, so the mean is 30/4 = 7.5. Sales above 7.5 occurred on Wednesday (11) and Thursday (8), which is 2 days.

questions.question: For the whole sales table (Pens 50, Books 30, Bags 20 over the four days), what percentage of all items sold were books?
questions.explanation: Grand total = 50 + 30 + 20 = 100 items. Books are 30 of 100 = 30%.

questions.question: A two-way table shows how 100 students travel to school. Grade 7: bus 20, walk 15, cycle 5. Grade 8: bus 30, walk 10, cycle 20. Of the students who cycle, what percentage are in Grade 8?
questions.explanation: Total cyclists = 5 + 20 = 25. Of those, 20 are in Grade 8, so 20/25 = 0.8 = 80%. The comparison is made within the cycling group, not out of all 100 students.

questions.question: Using the same two-way table (Grade 7: bus 20, walk 15, cycle 5; Grade 8: bus 30, walk 10, cycle 20), which grade has the higher proportion of bus riders?

options.B: Grade 7, because it has fewer students overall
options.C: Neither - both grades have exactly 50% bus riders
options.D: It cannot be determined from the table

questions.explanation: Grade 7 has 20 + 15 + 5 = 40 students, of whom 20 ride the bus: 20/40 = 50%. Grade 8 has 30 + 10 + 20 = 60 students, of whom 30 ride the bus: 30/60 = 50%. The raw counts differ but the proportions are equal.

questions.question: A two-way table of 250 people is partly blank. Under 30: likes tea 60, likes coffee ?, row total 110. Aged 30 or over: likes tea ?, likes coffee 55, row total 140. How many people aged 30 or over like tea, and what percentage of all coffee drinkers are under 30?

options.A: 85 people; 47.6% of coffee drinkers are under 30
options.B: 85 people; 33.3% of coffee drinkers are under 30
options.C: 50 people; 47.6% of coffee drinkers are under 30
options.D: 85 people; 20% of coffee drinkers are under 30

questions.explanation: Under 30 coffee = 110 - 60 = 50. Aged 30+ tea = 140 - 55 = 85. Total coffee drinkers = 50 + 55 = 105, and 50/105 = 0.476 = 47.6%.

questions.question: A table lists three rice packs: Pack A 2 kg for 180 rupees; Pack B 5 kg for 425 rupees; Pack C 8 kg for 720 rupees with 10% off the listed price. Which pack is cheapest per kilogram, and what is that price?
questions.explanation: Pack A: 180/2 = 90 rupees/kg. Pack B: 425/5 = 85 rupees/kg. Pack C: 10% off 720 is 648, and 648/8 = 81 rupees/kg. Pack C is cheapest at 81 rupees/kg - the discount must be applied before comparing.

questions.question: A Venn diagram of two overlapping circles shows: Maths only 18, the overlap 7, Science only 12. How many students take both Maths and Science?
questions.explanation: The overlapping region represents students in both sets. That region shows 7.

questions.question: In the same Venn diagram (Maths only 18, both 7, Science only 12), how many students take Maths altogether?
questions.explanation: The whole Maths circle includes the overlap: 18 + 7 = 25 students.

questions.question: The same Venn diagram (Maths only 18, both 7, Science only 12) is drawn inside a rectangle, with 5 students outside both circles. How many students are in the survey?
questions.explanation: Add every region, including the one outside the circles: 18 + 7 + 12 + 5 = 42 students.

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, 18 like tea, 14 like coffee and 6 like both. How many students like neither drink?
questions.explanation: Students liking at least one = 18 + 14 - 6 = 26. So 30 - 26 = 4 like neither. (Adding 18 + 14 without subtracting the overlap double-counts the 6.)

questions.question: Of 40 students, 25 play cricket, 20 play football and 8 play neither. How many play both sports?
questions.explanation: Students playing at least one sport = 40 - 8 = 32. By inclusion-exclusion, 25 + 20 - both = 32, so both = 45 - 32 = 13.

questions.question: In a class of 30 students, 18 like tea, 14 like coffee and 6 like both. If one student is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student likes tea but not coffee?
questions.explanation: Tea only = 18 - 6 = 12 students. Probability = 12/30 = 0.4.

questions.question: In a two-circle Venn diagram for sets A and B, which region represents the students who are in A but not in B, and how is its size found?

options.A: The overlap; its size is n(A) + n(B)
options.B: The crescent of circle A outside the overlap; its size is n(A) - n(A and B)
options.C: Everything inside circle B; its size is n(B) - n(A)
options.D: The area outside both circles; its size is the total minus n(A)

questions.explanation: 'In A but not B' is the part of circle A that does not overlap circle B. Removing the shared members from A gives n(A) - n(A and B).

questions.question: In a survey, n(A) = 45, n(B) = 52, n(C) = 38, n(A and B) = 20, n(B and C) = 18, n(A and C) = 15, and n(A and B and C) = 8. How many people are in A only?
questions.explanation: A only = n(A) - n(A and B) - n(A and C) + n(A and B and C) = 45 - 20 - 15 + 8 = 18. The triple overlap is added back because it was removed twice.

questions.question: Using the same values (n(A) = 45, n(B) = 52, n(C) = 38, n(A and B) = 20, n(B and C) = 18, n(A and C) = 15, n(A and B and C) = 8), how many of the 100 people surveyed belong to none of the three sets?
questions.explanation: n(A or B or C) = 45 + 52 + 38 - 20 - 18 - 15 + 8 = 90. So 100 - 90 = 10 people belong to none of the sets.

questions.question: In a survey of 100 people, n(A) = 45, n(B) = 52, n(C) = 38, n(A and B) = 20, n(B and C) = 18 and n(A and C) = 15. Exactly 6 people belong to none of the three sets. How many people belong to all three sets?
questions.explanation: If 6 belong to none, then n(A or B or C) = 100 - 6 = 94. Let the triple overlap be x: 45 + 52 + 38 - 20 - 18 - 15 + x = 82 + x = 94, so x = 12. The unknown sits inside the inclusion-exclusion formula and must be solved for.

questions.question: What is the mean of 4, 6, 8 and 10?
Five daily temperatures were recorded as 12, 15, 9, 14 and 10 degrees. What is the mean temperature?
The mean of four numbers is 20. Three of the numbers are 18, 22 and 15. What is the fourth number?
questions.explanation: The four numbers must total 4 x 20 = 80. The three known numbers total 55, so the fourth is 80 - 55 = 25.

questions.question: A shop sold 34, 41, 28, 45 and 52 ice creams on five days. The owner claims the daily average was more than 40. Is the claim correct?
questions.explanation: Sum = 34 + 41 + 28 + 45 + 52 = 200, so the mean is 200/5 = 40. Since 40 is not more than 40, the claim is not correct.

questions.question: A student's mean mark over 4 tests is 78. What must she score on her 5th test so that her mean over all 5 tests becomes 80?
questions.explanation: Current total = 4 x 78 = 312. Required total for a mean of 80 over 5 tests = 5 x 80 = 400. The 5th score must be 400 - 312 = 88.

questions.question: One class of 20 students has a mean score of 70. Another class of 30 students has a mean score of 80. What is the mean score of all 50 students?
questions.explanation: Totals: 20 x 70 = 1400 and 30 x 80 = 2400, giving 3800 altogether. Combined mean = 3800/50 = 76. (75 would be the answer only if the classes were the same size.)

questions.question: A set of numbers has a mean of 15. Every number in the set is multiplied by 3 and then decreased by 5. What is the mean of the new set?
questions.explanation: Applying the same linear rule to every value transforms the mean the same way: new mean = 3(15) - 5 = 45 - 5 = 40.

questions.question: The mean of 10 numbers is 24. Two of the numbers, whose mean is 15, are removed. What is the mean of the remaining 8 numbers?
questions.explanation: Total of all 10 = 10 x 24 = 240. The two removed numbers total 2 x 15 = 30. Remaining total = 210, so the mean is 210/8 = 26.25.

questions.question: The mean of 20 observations was calculated as 36. It was then found that one observation had been entered as 48 instead of its true value 84. What is the corrected mean?
questions.explanation: Recorded total = 20 x 36 = 720. The entry was 84 - 48 = 36 too small, so the corrected total is 756. Corrected mean = 756/20 = 37.8.

questions.question: Five distinct positive integers have a mean of 10 and a median of 9. What is the largest possible value of any one of these integers?
questions.explanation: The five numbers total 5 x 10 = 50, and the middle one is 9. To make the largest number as big as possible, make the others as small as possible: the two below the median are 1 and 2, and the fourth must be a distinct integer greater than 9, so at least 10. Then the largest = 50 - 1 - 2 - 9 - 10 = 28.

questions.question: What is the median of 3, 7, 9, 12, 15?
questions.explanation: The values are already in order and there are 5 of them, so the median is the middle (3rd) value: 9.

questions.question: What is the median of 4, 8, 10, 14?
questions.explanation: With an even count there is no single middle value, so average the two middle ones: (8 + 10)/2 = 9.

questions.question: What is the median of the data set 23, 11, 17, 9, 20?
questions.explanation: The data must be ordered first: 9, 11, 17, 20, 23. The middle value is 17. (Taking the middle of the unordered list would wrongly give 17 only by luck in other sets - ordering is the essential step.)

questions.question: Six houses on a street sold for 32, 35, 38, 41, 44 and 250 lakh rupees. What is the median selling price?
questions.explanation: With 6 ordered values the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (38 + 41)/2 = 39.5 lakh. The very large last value does not pull the median the way it pulls the mean.

questions.question: The numbers 5, 9, x, 17 are written in increasing order and their median is 12. What is x?
questions.explanation: With 4 values the median is (9 + x)/2. Setting (9 + x)/2 = 12 gives 9 + x = 24, so x = 15, which indeed lies between 9 and 17.

questions.question: A frequency table records the number of pets per household: 1 pet (3 households), 2 pets (5), 3 pets (8), 4 pets (4). What is the median number of pets?
questions.explanation: There are 3 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 20 households, so the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative frequencies are 3, 8, 16, 20, so both the 10th and 11th households have 3 pets. Median = 3.

questions.question: The nine values 12, 15, 18, 22, 26, 30, 34, 38, 45 have median 26. A tenth value, 50, is added. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: With 10 values the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th. Since 50 is added at the top end, the ordered list still has 26 in 5th place and 30 in 6th place, so the median = (26 + 30)/2 = 28.

questions.question: The annual salaries at a small firm are 3, 3.5, 4, 4.5 and 60 lakh rupees. Which statement best describes the situation?

options.A: The mean, 15 lakh, describes a typical salary better than the median
options.B: The median, 4 lakh, describes a typical salary better, because the single very high salary inflates the mean
options.C: The mean and the median are equally good because both are measures of centre
options.D: Neither measure can be calculated because of the outlier

questions.explanation: Mean = 75/5 = 15 lakh, but four of the five staff earn under 5 lakh, so the mean is misleading. The median of 4 lakh is resistant to the outlier and better represents a typical salary.

questions.question: Sixty test scores are grouped as 0-10: 5, 10-20: 12, 20-30: 18, 30-40: 15, 40-50: 10. Using the grouped-data median formula, what is the median score (to one decimal place)?
questions.explanation: n/2 = 30. Cumulative frequencies are 5, 17, 35, 50, 60, so the median class is 20-30 with lower boundary L = 20, preceding cumulative frequency cf = 17, class frequency f = 18 and width h = 10. Median = 20 + ((30 - 17)/18) x 10 = 20 + 7.22 = 27.2.

questions.question: A set of 8 numbers has a median of 21, and no number in the set equals 21. Every number greater than the median is increased by 10, and every number less than the median is decreased by 6. What is the new median?
questions.explanation: With 8 numbers the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th values. The 4th is below 21 so it drops by 6; the 5th is above 21 so it rises by 10. Neither change alters the ordering, so the new median = (old 4th - 6 + old 5th + 10)/2 = old median + 2 = 21 + 2 = 23.

questions.question: What is the mode of 3, 5, 5, 7, 9?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Only 5 appears more than once, so the mode is 5.

questions.question: Find the mode of 2, 4, 4, 6, 7, 7, 7, 9.
questions.explanation: The value 4 occurs twice but 7 occurs three times, which is more than any other value. The mode is 7.

questions.question: What is the mode of 1, 2, 2, 5, 7, 7, 9?
questions.explanation: Both 2 and 7 occur twice, and no value occurs more often. The data set is bimodal, so both 2 and 7 are modes.

questions.question: A shoe shop records the sizes sold in a day: 7, 8, 8, 6, 9, 8, 7, 10, 8, 9. The owner wants to know which size to stock most heavily. Which average should she use, and what is its value?
questions.explanation: Stocking decisions depend on which size sells most often, which is the mode. Size 8 appears four times, more than any other size.

questions.question: A frequency table shows the number of children per family: 1 child (4 families), 2 children (9 families), 3 children (6 families), 4 children (3 families). What is the modal number of children?
questions.explanation: The mode is the data value with the highest frequency, not the frequency itself. The largest frequency is 9, which belongs to the value 2.

questions.question: For the data 5, 7, 7, 8, 13, which statement is correct?

options.A: The mode and median are both 7, and the mean is larger than both
options.B: The mode, median and mean are all equal to 8
options.C: The mode is 7 and the mean is smaller than the median
options.D: The mode is 8 and the median is 7

questions.explanation: Mode = 7 (the only repeated value). With 5 ordered values the median is the 3rd, which is 7. Mean = 40/5 = 8, which is greater than 7.

questions.question: The data set 4, 4, 6, 8, 9, 9 currently has two modes. One more value is added and the set becomes 4, 4, 6, 8, 9, 9, 9. What happens to the mode and to the median?

options.A: The mode becomes 9 only, and the median stays 7
options.B: The mode becomes 9 only, and the median changes from 7 to 8
options.C: The set is still bimodal, and the median changes to 8
options.D: The mode becomes 4, and the median stays 7

questions.explanation: With three 9s, 9 is now the unique mode. Originally the median was (6 + 8)/2 = 7; with 7 values the median is the 4th value, which is 8.

questions.question: A frequency table shows scores 10 (frequency 5), 20 (frequency x), 30 (frequency 7) and 40 (frequency 4). It is known that 20 is the unique mode. What is the smallest possible value of x?
questions.explanation: For 20 to be the only mode, its frequency must be strictly greater than every other frequency. The largest other frequency is 7, so x must be at least 8.

questions.question: A set of 7 numbers has a mean of 14, and the value 12 is the mode, occurring exactly three times. What is the mean of the other four numbers?
questions.explanation: Total of all 7 numbers = 7 x 14 = 98. The three 12s contribute 36, leaving 98 - 36 = 62 for the other four numbers. Their mean is 62/4 = 15.5.

questions.question: Five positive integers have a mean of 9, a median of 8 and 8 as their only mode. What is the largest value the biggest of these integers can take?
questions.explanation: The five numbers total 5 x 9 = 45 and the middle one is 8. For 8 to be the unique mode it must appear at least twice. To maximise the largest number, make the others as small as possible: 1, 8, 8, 8 gives the largest = 45 - 1 - 8 - 8 - 8 = 20. Any other arrangement (for example 1, 8, 8, 9) leaves a smaller top value.

questions.question: What is the range of 4, 9, 15, 2, 11?
questions.explanation: Range = largest - smallest = 15 - 2 = 13.

questions.question: The midday temperatures on four days were -5, 3, 8 and -2 degrees Celsius. What is the range?
questions.explanation: Largest = 8, smallest = -5. Range = 8 - (-5) = 13 degrees. Subtracting a negative increases the result.

questions.question: The data set 7, 12, x, 20 has a range of 18, and x is the smallest value. What is x?
questions.explanation: The largest value is 20. If the range is 18, the smallest value is 20 - 18 = 2. Since x is the smallest, x = 2.

questions.question: A cricketer scored 42, 0, 67, 15, 88 and 23 runs in six innings. What is the range of his scores, and what does it tell you?

options.D: 88; his scores vary widely from innings to innings

questions.explanation: Range = 88 - 0 = 88 runs. A large range relative to the scores shows that his performance is very inconsistent. The range measures spread, not centre or best performance.

questions.question: A stem-and-leaf plot (stems are tens) reads: 2 | 4 7; 3 | 1 5 5 8; 4 | 0 6; 5 | 3. What is the range of the data?
questions.explanation: The smallest value is 24 and the largest is 53. Range = 53 - 24 = 29. The stems and leaves must be combined into full values first.

questions.question: Set P is 20, 22, 24, 26, 28 and set Q is 10, 18, 24, 30, 38. Compare the two sets.

options.A: They have the same mean, but Q has the larger range
options.B: They have the same range, but Q has the larger mean
options.C: P has both the larger mean and the larger range
options.D: They are identical in mean, median and range

questions.explanation: Both sets total 120, so both have mean 24. The range of P is 28 - 20 = 8, while the range of Q is 38 - 10 = 28. Equal centres can hide very different spreads.

questions.question: The salaries in a small office are 18, 20, 21, 22 and 95 (in thousands). Why might the range be a poor description of how spread out the typical salaries are?

options.A: Because the range uses only the two extreme values, and one unusually high salary makes it 77 even though four salaries lie within 4 of each other
options.B: Because the range can never be calculated when an outlier is present
options.C: Because the range is always smaller than the interquartile range
options.D: Because the range ignores the largest value in a data set

questions.explanation: Range = 95 - 18 = 77, driven entirely by the single outlier. Four of the five salaries lie between 18 and 22, so a measure such as the interquartile range describes the typical spread far better.

questions.question: A data set has a range of 14. Every value is multiplied by 3 and then 4 is added. What is the range of the new data set?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 3 multiplies all distances between values by 3, so the range becomes 42. Adding 4 shifts every value equally and does not change the spread at all.

questions.question: Data set A has a smallest value of 5 and a range of 12. Data set B has a smallest value of 20 and a range of 9. If the two sets are combined into one, what is the range of the combined set?
questions.explanation: A runs from 5 to 5 + 12 = 17. B runs from 20 to 20 + 9 = 29. The combined set has smallest value 5 and largest value 29, so the range is 29 - 5 = 24. Ranges cannot simply be added.

questions.question: Five positive integers have a mean of 12 and a range of 20, and the smallest of them is 4. What is the largest possible value of their median?
questions.explanation: The total is 5 x 12 = 60 and the largest value is 4 + 20 = 24, so the three middle numbers sum to 60 - 4 - 24 = 32. Writing them as b, c, d with 4 <= b <= c <= d <= 24, the median c is largest when b is as small as possible (b = 4), leaving c + d = 28 with c <= d, so c <= 14. The median can be at most 14 (for example 4, 4, 14, 14, 24).

questions.question: A boy has 3 shirts and 4 pairs of trousers. How many different shirt-and-trouser outfits can he make?
questions.explanation: By the multiplication principle, each of the 3 shirts can be paired with each of the 4 trousers: 3 x 4 = 12 outfits.

questions.question: A code is made of two digits, each chosen from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and digits may repeat. How many codes are possible?
questions.explanation: There are 5 choices for the first digit and, because repetition is allowed, 5 again for the second: 5 x 5 = 25 codes.

questions.question: In how many different orders can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
questions.explanation: This is an arrangement of all 4 distinct items: 4! = 4 x 3 x 2 x 1 = 24 orders.

questions.question: From a group of 5 students, one is to be chosen as president and a different one as vice-president. In how many ways can this be done?
questions.explanation: Order matters because the two posts are different. There are 5 choices for president and 4 remaining for vice-president: 5 x 4 = 20 ways.

questions.question: A teacher must choose 3 students from a class of 7 to form a team. The three roles are identical. In how many ways can the team be chosen?
questions.explanation: Order does not matter, so this is a combination: C(7,3) = (7 x 6 x 5)/(3 x 2 x 1) = 35. The answer 210 would count each team 6 times, once per ordering.

questions.question: A committee must contain exactly 2 boys chosen from 5 boys and exactly 2 girls chosen from 4 girls. How many different committees are possible?
questions.explanation: Boys: C(5,2) = 10. Girls: C(4,2) = 6. The two independent choices multiply: 10 x 6 = 60 committees.

questions.question: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if no digit may be repeated and the number cannot begin with 0?
questions.explanation: The leading digit has 5 choices (not 0). Then 5 digits remain for the second place (0 is now allowed) and 4 for the third: 5 x 5 x 4 = 100. Handling the restricted position first is the key strategy.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made of all the letters of the word LEVEL?
questions.explanation: LEVEL has 5 letters with L repeated twice and E repeated twice. The number of distinct arrangements is 5!/(2! x 2!) = 120/4 = 30. Treating the letters as all different would wrongly give 120.

questions.question: A team of 4 is chosen from 6 boys and 4 girls. How many teams contain at least one girl?
questions.explanation: Total teams = C(10,4) = 210. Teams with no girls (all boys) = C(6,4) = 15. Teams with at least one girl = 210 - 15 = 195. Counting the complement is far quicker than adding four separate cases.

questions.question: Six students stand in a row for a photograph. In how many arrangements are two particular students NOT standing next to each other?
questions.explanation: All arrangements = 6! = 720. Treating the two students as a single block gives 5! = 120 arrangements, and they can swap within the block, so 120 x 2 = 240 arrangements have them together. Not together = 720 - 240 = 480.

questions.question: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that both show heads?
questions.explanation: The outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT, all equally likely. Only HH has both heads, so the probability is 1/4.

questions.question: A fair coin is tossed and a fair six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a head and a 6?
questions.explanation: The events are independent, so multiply: P(head) x P(6) = 1/2 x 1/6 = 1/12.

questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the total is 7?
questions.explanation: There are 36 equally likely outcomes. Totals of 7 come from (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1) - six outcomes. So 6/36 = 1/6.

questions.question: A bag holds 4 red and 6 blue marbles. A marble is drawn, its colour noted, and it is put back before a second marble is drawn. What is the probability that both marbles are blue?
questions.explanation: With replacement the draws are independent and P(blue) stays 6/10 = 0.6 each time. P(both blue) = 0.6 x 0.6 = 0.36.

questions.question: A box contains 5 red and 3 blue pens. Two pens are taken out one after the other WITHOUT replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
questions.explanation: P(first red) = 5/8. After removing a red pen, 4 red remain out of 7, so P(second red) = 4/7. Multiplying: 5/8 x 4/7 = 20/56 = 5/14. (25/64 wrongly assumes replacement.)

questions.question: A single card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52. What is the probability that it is a king or a queen?
questions.explanation: A card cannot be both a king and a queen, so the events are mutually exclusive and the probabilities add: 4/52 + 4/52 = 8/52 = 2/13.

questions.question: In a class, P(a student plays cricket) = 0.6, P(a student plays chess) = 0.5 and P(a student plays both) = 0.3. What is the probability that a randomly chosen student plays at least one of the two games?
questions.explanation: The events overlap, so P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B) = 0.6 + 0.5 - 0.3 = 0.8. Simply adding would give 1.1, which is impossible for a probability.

questions.question: The probability of rain on any given day is 0.3, independently of other days. What is the probability that it rains on at least one of two consecutive days?
questions.explanation: P(no rain on a day) = 0.7, so P(no rain on either day) = 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49. P(at least one rainy day) = 1 - 0.49 = 0.51. The complement avoids adding several cases.

questions.question: Bag X holds 3 white and 2 black balls; bag Y holds 1 white and 4 black balls. A fair coin decides which bag is used (heads for X, tails for Y), and then one ball is drawn. What is the probability that the ball is white?
questions.explanation: P(white) = P(X) x P(white | X) + P(Y) x P(white | Y) = 0.5 x (3/5) + 0.5 x (1/5) = 0.3 + 0.1 = 0.4. Each branch of the tree must be weighted by the chance of taking that branch.

questions.question: A box has 4 green and 6 yellow balls. Three balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that at least one is green?
questions.explanation: P(no green) = P(all three yellow) = (6/10) x (5/9) x (4/8) = 120/720 = 1/6. So P(at least one green) = 1 - 1/6 = 5/6. Working with the complement replaces three separate cases with one calculation.

questions.question: A fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a 4?
questions.explanation: There is 1 favourable outcome out of 6 equally likely outcomes, so the probability is 1/6.

questions.question: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes = 4 red, total outcomes = 10 balls. P(red) = 4/10 = 0.4.

questions.question: For the same bag (4 red, 6 blue), what is the probability that a ball drawn at random is NOT red?
questions.explanation: Using the complement: P(not red) = 1 - P(red) = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6. This matches counting directly: 6 blue out of 10.

questions.question: A spinner is divided into 8 equal sectors: 3 are red, 2 are green, 2 are blue and 1 is yellow. What is the probability of landing on green or yellow?
questions.explanation: Favourable sectors = 2 green + 1 yellow = 3 out of 8 equal sectors, so the probability is 3/8.

questions.question: A table shows how 50 students travel to school: bus 22, cycle 13, walk 15. If one student is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student cycles, as a percentage?
questions.explanation: P(cycles) = 13/50 = 0.26 = 26%. Converting the fraction to a percentage requires multiplying by 100.

questions.question: A bag contains 40 balls, some green and the rest white. The probability of drawing a green ball is 3/8. How many white balls are in the bag?
questions.explanation: Green balls = (3/8) x 40 = 15, so white balls = 40 - 15 = 25. The reasoning runs backwards from the probability to a count.

questions.question: A coin is tossed 20 times and lands on heads 13 times. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The coin must be biased, because 13 is more than 10
options.B: The experimental probability of heads is 0.65, while the theoretical probability for a fair coin is 0.5; short runs often differ from theory
options.C: The theoretical probability of heads is now 0.65
options.D: The next toss is more likely to be a tail, to balance the results

questions.explanation: Experimental probability = 13/20 = 0.65, based on what happened. Theoretical probability for a fair coin stays 0.5. Small samples vary, and each toss remains independent of the previous ones.

questions.question: A box holds 5 red and 7 blue pens. How many extra red pens must be added so that the probability of drawing a red pen becomes 1/2?
questions.explanation: If x red pens are added, P(red) = (5 + x)/(12 + x) = 1/2. Cross-multiplying: 10 + 2x = 12 + x, so x = 2. Check: 7 red out of 14 pens is exactly 1/2.

questions.question: The probability that a machine produces a faulty item is 0.15. In a batch of 400 items, what is the expected number of faulty items, and can we be sure of that number?

options.A: 60 faulty items, and exactly 60 will always be faulty
options.B: 60 faulty items, but the actual number will vary around this value
options.C: 15 faulty items, but the actual number will vary
options.D: 85 faulty items, and this is only an estimate

questions.explanation: Expected number = 0.15 x 400 = 60. Expectation is a long-run average, so any particular batch may contain more or fewer than 60 faulty items.

questions.question: Cards numbered 1 to 30 are placed in a box and one is drawn at random. What is the probability that the number drawn is a multiple of 3 or a multiple of 5?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 3: 10 numbers. Multiples of 5: 6 numbers. Multiples of both (that is, of 15): 15 and 30, so 2 numbers counted twice. Favourable = 10 + 6 - 2 = 14, giving 14/30 = 7/15. Forgetting to subtract the overlap gives 16/30.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of any quadrilateral?
questions.explanation: A quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, so its interior angles total 2 x 180 = 360 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum = 180(n - 2) with n = 6: 180 x 4 = 720 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: What is the size of each interior angle of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: Sum = 180(5 - 2) = 540 degrees. In a regular pentagon all 5 angles are equal: 540/5 = 108 degrees. (72 degrees is the exterior angle.)

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: Three angles of a quadrilateral measure 85, 100 and 95 degrees. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explanation: The four angles total 360 degrees. The three given angles sum to 280, so the fourth is 360 - 280 = 80 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: The interior angles of a polygon add up to 1440 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Set 180(n - 2) = 1440, so n - 2 = 8 and n = 10. The polygon is a decagon.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle = 180 - 150 = 30 degrees. Exterior angles of any polygon total 360 degrees, so n = 360/30 = 12. Using the exterior angle is quicker than solving 180(n-2)/n = 150, which gives the same answer.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: The interior angles of a pentagon are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 5 : 6. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The angles total 180(5 - 2) = 540 degrees. The ratio has 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20 parts, so one part = 540/20 = 27 degrees. The five angles are 54, 81, 108, 135 and 162 degrees, which sum to 540. The largest is 162 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: In a regular polygon each interior angle is 4 times the size of each exterior angle. What is the sum of the interior angles of this polygon?
questions.explanation: Interior + exterior = 180, and interior = 4 x exterior, so 5 x exterior = 180 and exterior = 36 degrees. Then n = 360/36 = 10, and the interior sum = 180(10 - 2) = 1440 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: In a hexagon, four of the interior angles are each 130 degrees and the remaining two angles are equal to each other. What is the size of each of these two angles?
questions.explanation: The hexagon's angles total 180(6 - 2) = 720 degrees. The four known angles total 4 x 130 = 520 degrees, leaving 200 degrees for the two equal angles, so each is 100 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Interior Angles Figures with More than 3 Sides
questions.question: In a convex polygon, every interior angle measures 150 degrees except one, which measures 120 degrees. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.explanation: With n sides, (n - 1) angles are 150 degrees and one is 120 degrees, so 150(n - 1) + 120 = 180(n - 2). Expanding: 150n - 30 = 180n - 360, giving 30n = 330 and n = 11. Check: 10 x 150 + 120 = 1620 = 180 x 9.

questions.question: Two angles of a triangle are 50 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle total 180 degrees: 180 - (50 + 60) = 70 degrees.

questions.question: In a right-angled triangle, one of the acute angles is 35 degrees. What is the other acute angle?
questions.explanation: The right angle uses 90 degrees, leaving 90 degrees for the two acute angles. So the other is 90 - 35 = 55 degrees.

questions.question: An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of 40 degrees. What is the size of each base angle?
questions.explanation: The two base angles are equal and together make 180 - 40 = 140 degrees, so each is 140/2 = 70 degrees.

questions.question: A triangular garden plot has one angle of 90 degrees and another of 28 degrees. A gardener claims the third angle is obtuse. Is he right?

options.A: Yes, the third angle is 118 degrees
options.B: No, the third angle is 62 degrees, which is acute
options.C: No, the third angle is 90 degrees, which is a right angle
options.D: It cannot be decided without knowing the side lengths

questions.explanation: Third angle = 180 - 90 - 28 = 62 degrees, which is less than 90, so it is acute. A triangle can have at most one angle of 90 degrees or more.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the size of the largest angle?
questions.explanation: There are 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 parts sharing 180 degrees, so one part = 20 degrees. The angles are 40, 60 and 80 degrees, and the largest is 80 degrees.

questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle measures 120 degrees. One of the two non-adjacent interior angles is 45 degrees. What is the other non-adjacent interior angle?
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 120 = 45 + x, so x = 75 degrees.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are x, (2x - 10) and (x + 30) degrees. What type of triangle is it?

options.B: Isosceles, with two angles of 70 degrees

questions.explanation: x + (2x - 10) + (x + 30) = 180 gives 4x + 20 = 180, so x = 40. The angles are 40, 70 and 70 degrees - two equal angles, so the triangle is isosceles.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = AC and angle A = 50 degrees. Side BC is extended to point D. What is the size of angle ACD?
questions.explanation: Since AB = AC, angles B and C are equal: each is (180 - 50)/2 = 65 degrees. Angle ACD is the exterior angle at C, so it is 180 - 65 = 115 degrees (equivalently 50 + 65).

questions.question: In triangle PQR, angle P = 64 degrees. The bisectors of angles Q and R meet at point I. What is the size of angle QIR?
questions.explanation: Angles Q + R = 180 - 64 = 116 degrees, so half of Q plus half of R = 58 degrees. In triangle QIR, angle QIR = 180 - 58 = 122 degrees. (This matches the rule 90 + P/2 = 90 + 32.)

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angle B is 20 degrees larger than angle A, and angle C is equal to the sum of angles A and B. What is the size of angle A?
questions.explanation: Let A = a, so B = a + 20 and C = a + (a + 20) = 2a + 20. Then a + (a + 20) + (2a + 20) = 180, giving 4a + 40 = 180 and a = 35. The angles are 35, 55 and 90 degrees, which sum to 180.

questions.question: Two triangles have all three pairs of corresponding sides equal. Which congruence criterion proves they are congruent?
questions.explanation: Three pairs of equal sides is the side-side-side (SSS) criterion.

questions.question: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle PQR. Which side of triangle PQR has the same length as side AC?
questions.explanation: In the statement ABC = PQR, A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R. So AC matches PR.

questions.question: In two triangles, two pairs of sides are equal and the angles BETWEEN those pairs of sides are also equal. Which criterion applies?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the included angle is the side-angle-side (SAS) criterion. The angle must lie between the two sides for SAS to apply.

questions.question: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, AB = 7 cm and angle B = 55 degrees. In triangle DEF, EF = 9 cm. What are the lengths of DE and the size of angle E?
questions.explanation: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal. AB corresponds to DE, so DE = 7 cm, and angle B corresponds to angle E, so angle E = 55 degrees.

questions.question: In triangles ABC and DEF: angle A = angle D = 40 degrees, angle B = angle E = 75 degrees, and AB = DE = 6 cm. Are the triangles congruent, and by which criterion?

options.D: No, angles alone cannot prove congruence

questions.explanation: The side AB lies between angles A and B, and DE lies between angles D and E. Two angles with the included side equal is the ASA criterion, so the triangles are congruent.

questions.question: Two triangles have all three pairs of angles equal. What can be concluded?

options.B: They are similar but not necessarily congruent, because equal angles fix shape but not size
options.C: They are neither similar nor congruent
options.D: They are congruent only if all angles are 60 degrees

questions.explanation: Equal angles guarantee the same shape, so the triangles are similar. Without any side equal, one could be an enlargement of the other, so congruence does not follow. AAA is not a congruence criterion.

questions.question: In quadrilateral ABCD, AB = CD and BC = DA. The diagonal AC is drawn. Why are triangles ABC and CDA congruent, and what follows?

options.A: By SSS, since AC is common to both; it then follows that angle B = angle D
options.B: By SAS, since angle B = angle D is given; it then follows that AC = BD
options.C: By ASA, since the diagonal bisects the angles; it then follows that AB is parallel to BC
options.D: They are not congruent, because no angle information is given

questions.explanation: AB = CD, BC = DA and AC = CA (the shared diagonal), so the triangles are congruent by SSS. Corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal, so angle B = angle D.

questions.question: In triangles ABC and PQR you already know AB = PQ and angle A = angle P. Which ONE extra piece of information is NOT enough on its own to prove the triangles congruent?
questions.explanation: AC = PR gives SAS (the angle is included). angle B = angle Q gives ASA, and angle C = angle R gives AAS, both valid. BC = QR gives two sides and a non-included angle (SSA), which is not a valid congruence criterion.

questions.question: Segments AB and CD cross at point O, with AO = OB and CO = OD. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Triangles AOC and BOD are congruent by SAS, using vertically opposite angles at O, so AC = BD
options.B: Triangles AOC and BOD are congruent by SSS, so AC = BD
options.C: The triangles cannot be congruent because no angle is given
options.D: Triangles AOC and BOD are congruent by ASA, so AO = CO

questions.explanation: AO = OB and CO = OD are given, and angle AOC = angle BOD because they are vertically opposite. That included angle makes it SAS, and corresponding parts then give AC = BD.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, AB = AC. Point D lies on BC so that AD is perpendicular to BC. Which chain of reasoning correctly shows that D is the midpoint of BC?

options.A: Triangles ABD and ACD share AD, have AB = AC and right angles at D, so they are congruent by RHS; hence BD = DC
options.B: Triangles ABD and ACD are congruent by SSS, because BD = DC is given
options.C: Triangles ABD and ACD are congruent by AAA, so BD = DC
options.D: D cannot be shown to be the midpoint without knowing the length of BC

questions.explanation: The hypotenuses AB and AC are equal, AD is a common side, and both triangles have a right angle at D. That is the RHS criterion, and corresponding parts then give BD = DC, so D is the midpoint. Option B assumes the very thing being proved.

questions.question: What is the complement of a 35 degree angle?
questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees: 90 - 35 = 55 degrees.

questions.question: What is the supplement of a 110 degree angle?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees: 180 - 110 = 70 degrees.

questions.question: An angle's supplement is three times the angle itself. What is the angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angle be a. Then 180 - a = 3a, so 180 = 4a and a = 45 degrees. Check: the supplement is 135, which is 3 x 45.

questions.question: A ray stands on a straight line, forming two angles on one side. One of them measures 118 degrees. What is the other, and what is this pair called?
questions.explanation: Angles on a straight line add to 180 degrees, so the other is 180 - 118 = 62 degrees, and a pair summing to 180 is called supplementary.

questions.question: Two complementary angles measure (2x + 10) and 3x degrees. What are the two angles?
questions.explanation: (2x + 10) + 3x = 90 gives 5x + 10 = 90, so x = 16. The angles are 2(16) + 10 = 42 and 3(16) = 48 degrees, which add to 90.

questions.question: The supplement of an angle is 40 degrees more than three times its complement. What is the angle?
questions.explanation: Let the angle be a. Then 180 - a = 3(90 - a) + 40 = 310 - 3a, so 2a = 130 and a = 65 degrees. Check: the supplement is 115, the complement is 25, and 3(25) + 40 = 115.

questions.question: Which statement about angle pairs is always true?

options.A: Two obtuse angles can be supplementary
options.B: Two acute angles can be supplementary
options.C: If two angles are complementary, both must be acute
options.D: An angle and its supplement are always both acute

questions.explanation: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees, so neither can reach 90 degrees; both must be acute. Two obtuse angles would exceed 180, and two acute angles total less than 180, so neither can be supplementary.

questions.question: Three angles lie side by side on one side of a straight line. The first is a right angle, the second is 43 degrees, and the third is unknown. What is the third angle, and what is its complement?
questions.explanation: The three angles total 180 degrees, so the third is 180 - 90 - 43 = 47 degrees. Its complement is 90 - 47 = 43 degrees.

questions.question: Two supplementary angles are in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the complement of the smaller of the two angles?

options.D: The smaller angle has no complement

questions.explanation: The ratio has 9 parts sharing 180 degrees, so one part = 20 degrees and the angles are 80 and 100 degrees. The smaller is 80 degrees, and its complement is 90 - 80 = 10 degrees.

questions.question: Angle P and angle Q are complementary, and the supplement of angle P is 20 degrees larger than the supplement of angle Q. What is the supplement of angle Q?
questions.explanation: Since P + Q = 90, we have Q = 90 - P. The supplement of P is 180 - P, and the supplement of Q is 180 - (90 - P) = 90 + P. The condition gives 180 - P = (90 + P) + 20, so 70 = 2P and P = 35. Then Q = 55 and its supplement is 180 - 55 = 125 degrees. (145 degrees is the supplement of P, not of Q.)

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle measures 70 degrees. What is the size of the corresponding angle at the other intersection?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so the angle is also 70 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and one interior angle is 58 degrees. What is the alternate interior angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles on parallel lines are equal, so the angle is 58 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One co-interior (allied) angle is 115 degrees. What is the other co-interior angle?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary: 180 - 115 = 65 degrees. They are equal only when both are 90 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. At the upper intersection, one angle is 65 degrees. Which list correctly gives the sizes of all eight angles formed?

options.A: Four angles of 65 degrees and four of 115 degrees
options.C: Two angles of 65 degrees and six of 115 degrees
options.D: Four angles of 65 degrees and four of 25 degrees

questions.explanation: Each intersection produces two angles of 65 degrees (vertically opposite) and two of 180 - 65 = 115 degrees. Because the lines are parallel, the same pattern repeats at the second intersection, giving four of each.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of alternate interior angles measure (3x + 10) and (5x - 30) degrees. What is the size of each angle?
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal: 3x + 10 = 5x - 30, so 40 = 2x and x = 20. Each angle = 3(20) + 10 = 70 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. A pair of co-interior angles measure (2x + 20) and (3x + 10) degrees. What is the larger of the two angles?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles are supplementary: (2x + 20) + (3x + 10) = 180 gives 5x + 30 = 180 and x = 30. The angles are 80 and 100 degrees, so the larger is 100 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: A transversal cuts two lines. A pair of co-interior angles measure 105 degrees and 80 degrees. What can you conclude?

options.A: The lines are parallel, because the angles are both obtuse
options.B: The lines are not parallel, because co-interior angles would have to sum to 180 degrees
options.C: The lines are parallel, because the angles are unequal
options.D: Nothing can be concluded without more information

questions.explanation: Co-interior angles sum to 180 degrees exactly when the lines are parallel. Here 105 + 80 = 185, not 180, so the lines cannot be parallel. The test runs in reverse: the angle relation proves or disproves parallelism.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Lines AB and CD are parallel. A point P lies between them, forming a zigzag. Angle between PA and line AB is 35 degrees, and the angle between PC and line CD is 48 degrees. What is angle APC?
questions.explanation: Draw a line through P parallel to AB and CD. It splits angle APC into two parts, which equal 35 degrees and 48 degrees by alternate interior angles. So angle APC = 35 + 48 = 83 degrees. The auxiliary parallel line is the method that must be chosen.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle measures (4x - 30) degrees, and the co-interior angle on the same side of the transversal measures (x + 45) degrees. What are the two angles?
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary: (4x - 30) + (x + 45) = 180, so 5x + 15 = 180 and x = 33. The angles are 4(33) - 30 = 102 degrees and 33 + 45 = 78 degrees, which add to 180. Assuming the angles were equal would wrongly give two angles of 102 degrees.

questions.skill_name: Angles on Parallel Lines Cut by a Transversal
questions.question: Lines l and m are parallel. A transversal crosses them, and the bisectors of a pair of co-interior angles are drawn. What is the angle between these two bisectors?

options.D: It depends on the size of the original angles

questions.explanation: Let the co-interior angles be a and b with a + b = 180. The bisectors make angles a/2 and b/2 with the transversal, and a/2 + b/2 = 90. In the triangle formed by the two bisectors and the transversal, the third angle is 180 - 90 = 90 degrees. The result is always a right angle, whatever the original angles.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has legs of 3 cm and 4 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem, h squared = 3 squared + 4 squared = 9 + 16 = 25, so h = 5 cm.

questions.question: In a right triangle the two shorter sides are 6 m and 8 m. Find the hypotenuse.
questions.explanation: h squared = 36 + 64 = 100, so h = 10 m. (100 is the square of the hypotenuse, not the hypotenuse itself.)

questions.question: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 13 cm and one leg of 5 cm. What is the other leg?
questions.explanation: Here the unknown is a leg, so subtract: leg squared = 13 squared - 5 squared = 169 - 25 = 144, giving 12 cm. Adding instead of subtracting is the common error.

questions.question: A 10 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 6 m from the base of the wall. How far up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse. Height squared = 10 squared - 6 squared = 100 - 36 = 64, so the ladder reaches 8 m up the wall.

questions.question: A rectangular field measures 12 m by 16 m. A path is laid along the diagonal. How long is the path?
questions.explanation: A diagonal splits the rectangle into two right triangles with legs 12 and 16. Diagonal squared = 144 + 256 = 400, so the path is 20 m.

questions.question: Which set of side lengths forms a right-angled triangle?
questions.explanation: Use the converse of the theorem: check whether the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two. 8 squared + 15 squared = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17 squared. None of the other sets satisfies this.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle has sides of 10 cm. What is the length of its altitude, correct to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The altitude bisects the base, creating a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and one leg 5. Altitude squared = 100 - 25 = 75, so the altitude = square root of 75 = 8.66 cm. Recognising that the altitude bisects the base is the key step.

questions.question: A hiker walks 15 km east, then 8 km north, then 9 km west. How far is she from her starting point?
questions.explanation: Net eastward displacement = 15 - 9 = 6 km; net northward = 8 km. Distance squared = 36 + 64 = 100, so she is 10 km away. The three legs must be resolved into two perpendicular displacements first.

questions.question: A closed box measures 12 cm by 4 cm by 3 cm. What is the length of the longest straight rod that can fit inside it?
questions.explanation: The longest rod lies along the space diagonal. First the base diagonal: 12 squared + 4 squared = 160. Then the space diagonal: 160 + 3 squared = 169, so the rod is 13 cm. The theorem is applied twice, in two perpendicular planes.

questions.question: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 25 cm, and one leg is 5 cm longer than the other. What is the perimeter of the triangle?
questions.explanation: Let the shorter leg be x, so the other is x + 5. Then x squared + (x + 5) squared = 625, giving 2x squared + 10x - 600 = 0, or x squared + 5x - 300 = 0. This factorises as (x + 20)(x - 15) = 0, so x = 15. The sides are 15, 20 and 25, and the perimeter is 60 cm.

questions.question: A net is made of six identical squares joined edge to edge. Which solid does it fold into?

options.C: A rectangular prism with different edge lengths

questions.explanation: Six identical square faces fold into a cube, the only solid whose faces are six congruent squares.

questions.question: A net consists of two identical circles and one rectangle. Which solid does it form?
questions.explanation: The two circles become the flat top and bottom, and the rectangle wraps around to form the curved surface of a cylinder.

questions.question: A net has one square with a triangle attached to each of its four sides. What solid does it make, and how many vertices does that solid have?
questions.explanation: The four triangles fold up to meet at a single apex above the square base, forming a square pyramid. It has 4 base vertices plus the apex, so 5 in all.

questions.question: How many faces of each kind appear in the net of a triangular prism?
questions.explanation: A triangular prism has two triangular ends and three rectangular side faces, so its net contains 2 triangles and 3 rectangles - five faces altogether.

questions.question: A net is made of six squares, each with side 5 cm. What is the total surface area of the solid it forms?
questions.explanation: Each square has area 5 x 5 = 25 square cm, and there are six of them: 6 x 25 = 150 square cm. (125 is the volume of the cube, not its surface area.)

questions.question: A cylinder has radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. In its net, what are the dimensions of the rectangle, and what is the total surface area? (Use pi = 22/7.)

options.A: Rectangle 44 cm by 10 cm; total surface area 748 square cm
options.B: Rectangle 22 cm by 10 cm; total surface area 528 square cm
options.C: Rectangle 44 cm by 10 cm; total surface area 440 square cm
options.D: Rectangle 7 cm by 10 cm; total surface area 224 square cm

questions.explanation: The rectangle's length equals the circumference: 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm, and its height is 10 cm, giving area 440 square cm. Each circular end has area (22/7) x 49 = 154 square cm. Total = 440 + 2(154) = 748 square cm.

questions.question: Six squares are arranged in a single straight row, joined edge to edge. Why will this arrangement NOT fold into a cube?

options.A: Because a cube needs eight squares, not six
options.B: Because folding the strip makes the squares wrap around and overlap, leaving two faces uncovered
options.C: Because the squares must all be different sizes
options.D: Because a cube's net must be a rectangle

questions.explanation: A cube does need exactly six squares, but their arrangement matters. Folding a straight strip of six wraps it around the cube like a belt: some squares land on top of each other while the top and bottom faces stay open.

questions.question: In a cube net shaped like a cross, the centre square is labelled 1, the four squares attached to its sides are labelled 2, 3, 4 and 5 going clockwise, and the square attached beyond square 3 is labelled 6. When folded, which face is opposite face 1?
questions.explanation: Squares 2, 3, 4 and 5 fold up to become the four sides around face 1, so none of them can be opposite it. Face 6, attached one step beyond face 3, folds over the top and lands directly opposite face 1. In any cube net, opposite faces are separated by exactly one square in a row.

questions.question: The net of a closed rectangular box contains two rectangles measuring 8 cm by 5 cm, two measuring 8 cm by 3 cm, and two measuring 5 cm by 3 cm. What are the dimensions of the box and its volume?

options.A: 8 by 5 by 3 cm; volume 120 cubic cm
options.B: 8 by 5 by 3 cm; volume 158 cubic cm
options.C: 16 by 10 by 6 cm; volume 960 cubic cm
options.D: 8 by 8 by 5 cm; volume 320 cubic cm
